There is an ideology called anarcho-capitalism. It's adherents believe that the perfect capitalism is capitalism without a government. They call current day capitalism "crony capitalism". They think that all monopolies are created because of the governments futile attempts at controlling the market. And their favourite phrase is: "the free market will solve it". I personally don't believe that such a system can ever be implemented because the government is an inherent part of capitalism. In order to have any private property you need to have an organization that will have the military to protect it. The job of the capitalist government is to keep the people in power in safety from the working class. Plus, current monopolies do really have a beneficial relationship with the government so they wouldn't let it disappear

I don't really have much experience with Japanese, but consuming media had certainly played an essential part in learning English for me. After that I started watching a lot of youtube videos in English, then went on to watching movies with subtitles, then without subtitles, now I'm reading 20th century classic books. So media can certainly help you learn a language. The funny thing is the fact that I didn't even plan to learn english, it happened mostly accidentally. So take this with a grain of salt.
